display_name: The Hebrew-canonical twin of the `legalese` row: the same drink-driving thresholds on the rule-effective-time axis, with every identifier, section title and herald in the instruments' own Hebrew

derived_from.relation: HAND-WRITTEN twin, held to the English row mechanically. ../../source/twin-check.py tokenises each English module and its Hebrew twin, drops comments and herald text, maps the English tokens through glossary.json and requires the two token streams to be identical: the rows may differ in names, comments and heralds and in nothing else. check.sh then runs both rows and requires every Result block to be identical after mapping this row's names back. The English row is the ORACLE; a disagreement is repaired here or in glossary.json.
derived_from.agreement_check: check.sh sections 1 and 3; also run from ../legalese/check.sh.

language.note: Identifiers, record fields, enum constructors, § titles, @nlg heralds and the statute-quoting comments are Hebrew; the maintainer's commentary is Hebrew in the module headers and English in NOTES.md. The binary this was checked on predates `@lang` and `l4 nlg --lang`, so the heralds are untagged and there is one language per row.

filenames.basenames: Latin, with a -he suffix, NOT Hebrew.
filenames.why: il/hvac-work-licensing-2025/encodings/legalese-he/NOTES.md section 4 measured that an IMPORT of a Hebrew basename resolves to nothing, silently. Not re-measured here; the workaround is inherited.

scope: As ../legalese/encoding.json, unchanged: this row decides nothing the English row does not decide.

verification.result: check.sh exit 0 on 2026-09-22: 0 errors, 30 of 30 assertions satisfied, both modules token-identical to the English ones through the glossary, 34 Result blocks identical.

not_reviewed.note: Two gaps with two reviewers. (1) The LAW is unreviewed: everything ../legalese/encoding.json says applies here unchanged. (2) The HEBREW is unreviewed: whether סף is the right noun for the pair of figures, whether הרכב שבו נהג is idiomatic, no mechanical check reaches. What has been checked is that the Hebrew lexes, parses, type-checks, evaluates, and returns the same answers as the English row. glossary.json marks every name ordinance, regulations or composed; the composed ones are where a Hebrew reviewer should start.

forks.F1-F5: Inherited from ../legalese; this row may not decide anything they leave open.
